questions.stem: Acute pain in the scrotum started two hours ago. The next-morning ultrasound slot is open. Next step?

options.text: Book that morning slot and send them home
Imaging now, and call the surgeon now
A clinic visit next week, if it still hurts
Antibiotics alone, and no examination

questions.explanation: A next-morning ultrasound is a delay. If a twisted testis is the worry, a scan must not delay the operating room.

questions.stem: A man has a painfully full bladder from prostate enlargement. First step?

options.text: A relaxing pill alone, and no catheter
A catheter now, then consider the relaxing pill after the bladder is empty
Finasteride tonight, as the emptying drug
Watch until morning clinic

questions.explanation: Catheterize now. The relaxing pill is started after the bladder is empty, not instead of emptying it.

questions.stem: The relaxing pill for prostate enlargement, given alone for a painful, full bladder:

options.text: Is what empties the bladder tonight
Is not what empties the bladder tonight
Replaces a recorded residual
Replaces kidney-number checks after prolonged retention

questions.explanation: That pill is not what empties the bladder tonight.

questions.stem: A febrile patient has an inflamed, tender gallbladder. The plan is:

options.text: Antibiotics alone and a clinic visit
Antibiotics and a surgery consult, with early surgery if the patient is fit
Discharge on pills and a goodbye
A relaxing prostate pill

questions.explanation: Antibiotics alone are not definitive therapy. Early cholecystectomy is for fit patients.

questions.stem: Jaundice or shock with suspected gallbladder infection suggests:

options.text: A routine clinic follow-up only
The stone may be in the duct, and that is a different procedure
That antibiotics can be skipped
That imaging can wait until morning

questions.explanation: Jaundice and hypotension move the plan toward the duct, not gallbladder removal alone.

questions.stem: When you treat pelvic inflammatory disease, the partner:

options.text: Can be ignored if the patient feels better
Is treated in the same plan
Is treated only if a Pap smear is abnormal
Waits for a culture from next month

questions.explanation: A prescription for one person is not the regimen. Treat the partner in the same plan.

questions.stem: Before the first dose for pelvic inflammatory disease, you should have:

options.text: A routine Pap result only
A pregnancy test result
A morning ultrasound of the scrotum
A six-week back scan

questions.explanation: A pregnancy test is resulted before the first dose.

questions.stem: Two days of ordinary low back pain, no warning signs. Imaging?

options.text: A magnetic scan today, routinely
No. Send them home without a scan, and write the warning signs that should bring them back
Bed rest for a month, then a scan
Opioids as the default prescription, and no advice

questions.explanation: Uncomplicated back pain goes home without a scan. Advise them to keep moving, not to stay in bed.

questions.stem: New saddle numbness and new bladder loss with back pain. Next step?

options.text: Home without a scan
Those signs cancel the discharge and start a scan today
A clinic visit in six weeks
A prostate-relaxing pill only

questions.explanation: Warning signs cancel the discharge and start a scan today.

questions.stem: One side of the face suddenly drooped this morning. The eye will not close. The plan includes:

options.text: An antiviral alone, with no steroid
A steroid today, within three days of onset, and a plan for the eye, including at night
Waiting a week to see if it improves, with no eye care
A next-morning ultrasound of the face

questions.explanation: A steroid today, and eye care. An antiviral is not a substitute for the steroid.
